summary: Logistics for the second network graphics meeting at Stanford, including a motel, a banquet, travel pooling and what to tell the organizers when registering.

plainLanguage.summary: Practical details for a meeting: where to stay, dinner plans and who to tell you are coming.

subtitle: Logistics for the second network graphics meeting at Stanford

tldr.problem: The Network Graphics Group needs to coordinate travel, accommodation and meals for a meeting at Stanford.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 253 announces the venue (Stanford AI Lab), accommodation (Flamingo Motel at $8.25/night), and a banquet (Monday, November 22 at the Golden Pavillion, $7.20/plate), and requests attendee information.
tldr.outcome: Attendees register with their requirements so organizers can arrange rooms, meals and transportation pools.

today: This was a logistics announcement for a 1971 meeting. It is historical documentation of early network research community organization.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 253 announces the second meeting of the Network Graphics Group, to be held at Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. The conference itself will be in the AI Lab conference room; attendees will stay at the Flamingo Motel in nearby Palo Alto, about 2 miles away.
sections.plainLanguage: Computer scientists working on graphics will meet at Stanford from November 21-23, 1971.

sections.title: Accommodation and Meals
sections.content: Rooms at the Flamingo Motel are $8.25 per night. Monday, November 22, a Chinese banquet will be held at the Golden Pavilion restaurant in Los Altos at $7.20 per plate. Non-network guests are welcome to attend the banquet if invited by attendees. The conference runs from 6:00 PM Sunday, November 21, through noon Tuesday, November 23, Pacific time.
sections.plainLanguage: A motel room costs $8.25, and the Monday dinner is $7.20 per person.

sections.title: Registration
sections.content: Attendees must notify Stanford as soon as possible with the following information: name, affiliation (site), whether a room is needed, whether they will attend the banquet, whether they will rent a car (for transportation pool coordination), and whether they plan to give a talk (with length and audio-visual requirements). This information can be sent to James A. Moorer, Stanford AI Lab, (405) 321-2300, extension 4971, or to the conference secretaries.
sections.plainLanguage: Tell Stanford if you are coming, if you need a bed, if you want dinner, and if you will need a rental car.

sections.title: Deadline and Maps
sections.content: The latest withdrawal date for banquet and room reservations is November 18; reservations after that date are considered binding. Maps will be sent to non-resident attendees as they register.
sections.plainLanguage: You must decide by November 18 if you are definitely coming. Stanford will send maps to visitors.

references.text: Postel, J. B., "Status of Network Graphics RFC", RFC 246.
